newsitem.title: FRANCE: Franco-Italian chipmaker SGS-Thomson issues warning.
newsitem.headline: Franco-Italian chipmaker SGS-Thomson issues warning.

text.p: Franco-Italian semiconductor group SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV Wednesday reported a 19 percent rise in 1996 earnings to $625.5 million but warned about the first quarter of 1997 after a weak end to last year.
The profit warning and lower fourth-quarter results took the market by surprise and the stock closed nearly 12 percent lower.
At SGS-Thomson, the fourth quarter earnings were down 15.5 percent to $142 million.

President and Chief Executive Pasquale Pistorio said he was pleased with the 1996 performance. He was cautious about the first quarter of 1997, although he said the company would still outperform the industry average.
"With lead times shrinking throughout the industry, we are entering the first quarter of 1997 with less order visibility than we have historically enjoyed," he said.

"From what we know today, we expect 1997 first-quarter revenues to be close to third quarter 1996 levels. We also anticipate that overall pricing pressures will continue, and therefore, in spite of productivity improvements, gross margins could be slightly below fourth quarter 1996 levels."
In the third quarter, net revenues were $988.4 million.

"While first quarter conditions continue to be uncertain, we believe that subsequent quarters of 1997 will show progressive improvement compared to the 1997 first quarter as the company continues to emphasise differentiated products and high growth applications," Pistorio added.
Company chief economist Jean-Phillipe Dauvin said the world semiconductor market had fallen by 8 percent in 1996, making it the third-worst year on record for the industry.
The fall was to a large extent due to price pressures, with prices of Dynamic Random Access Memory chips plunging by 80 to 90 percent, causing losses at many chipmakers.
SGS-Thomson does not make DRAMs. It makes dedicated chips, which shielded it somewhat from the price erosion, and its market rose by f5 percent.
Dauvin said that market research bureaus WSTS, Dataquest and VLSI Research were predicting a 1997 market increase ranging from respectively 7.4 percent to 14.9 percent.
